newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat steepens fall on views of ample supply.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat steepens fall on views of ample supply.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil accelerated its decline Thursday afternoon on views of ample supply amid bearish temperature forecasts, pressuring the rest of the oil complex, traders said.
"There is some fund selling, and it's related to weakness in the (U.S.) Gulf, and the temperature forecasts are now weighing in," said a refined products trader.

Late session, prompt heat broke support of 59.55 cents, what had been its low for the week. At 1434 EST, March heating oil was off 1.15 cents a gallon at 59.70 cents, hovering above its session low of 59.45.
U.S. Gulf heating oil and diesel cash prices slackened after tighter supplies due to a spate of refinery maintenance had firmed prices there recently.
But, on Thursday, refineries began to announce their return from seasonal turnaround.
Lyondell-Citgo, in particular, started up a $1.1 billion upgrade at its Houston refinery Wednesday with the plant running near design capacity of 235,000 barrels a day.
March gasoline was off 0.09 cent a gallon at 62.80 cents while March crude was off six cents at $21.80 a barrel.

The National Weather Service's six to 10 day forecast starting February 18 called for seasonally warm temperatures in the U.S. Northeast which has the largest concentration of heating oil users in the world.
The March heating oil-to-crude crack spread fell to $3.11 a barrel from $3.70 Wednesday.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
